text.p: These are the leading stories in the Moroccan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Messages exchanged by King Hassan and Algerian President Liamine Zeroual revive relations between the two countries which have been dormant for months.
- Morocco doing well financially after a year marked by 11.8 percent growth in real Gross Domestic Product, with the outlook seeming good for 1997.
- Tourism ministry strikes 13 hotels or restaurants from official list, downgrades 64, upgrades 18, and keeps 360 unchanged.
- Moroccan National Office of Tourism responsibilities to be transferred to Moroccan House for Tourism.
- Five living abandoned babies and six bodies of newly-born babies found between January 11 and 24 in Morocco.
- Central Bank puts in order credit purchases of private individuals.
- Cabinet hears summary of economy at end of 1996, seen as on the whole favourable.
- Office responsible for drinking water supplies seeks authority to increase bills by 12 percent but which will exempt 43 percent of households which are economically disadvantaged.
